content: Lisinopril is used in combination with hydrochlorothiazide to treat hypertension (high blood pressure), which helps lower blood pressure and reduce the risk of fatal and non-fatal cardiovascular events, such as strokes and myocardial infarctions [doc name, page 5]. This fixed-dose combination is not indicated for initial therapy [doc name, page 5].

Taking 5 times the prescribed dosage of lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide could lead to severe hypotension (low blood pressure) and electrolyte imbalances (e.g., hypokalemia, hypochloremia, hyponatremia) due to excessive diuresis and drug toxicity [doc name, page 19]. Overdose management includes discontinuing the medication, inducing emesis/gastric lavage, correcting dehydration and electrolyte disturbances, and administering intravenous normal saline for hypotension [doc name, page 19]. Hemodialysis may be used to remove lisinopril but is not specifically mentioned for hydrochlorothiazide overdose. Immediate medical attention is critical.
